subject: Information Theory
title: Code Rate and Overhead
description: Learn Code Rate and Overhead in one minute.

hook.text: A rate 1/2 code doubles your data. Half the bits are redundancy. Is that too much? It depends on the channel.

buildup.text: Code rate R = k/n, where k is data bits and n is total bits. Higher rate means less redundancy, less protection.

discovery.text: Shannon's theorem: as long as R < C (channel capacity), codes exist that make errors vanishingly rare.

twist.text: A code with rate above capacity will always have errors, no matter how clever the design. Shannon's bound is absolute.

climax.text: Engineers choose code rate by balancing bandwidth cost against error tolerance. It's a core design decision.

punchline.text: Rate versus reliability. Every system picks a point on the curve.

quiz.question: What does a code rate of 1/2 mean?
options: Half the transmitted bits carry actual data, half are redundancy
The code corrects half of all errors
